claim: WatchGuard's current Mobile VPN with SSL client 2026.2.1 is published only for Windows and macOS, released 07/02/2026; no Linux download exists.
quote: Mobile VPN with SSL 2026.2.1 for Windows ... Mobile VPN with SSL 2026.2.1 for MacOS ... 07/02/2026

claim: WatchGuard's client install documentation covers Windows and macOS only; Linux is not mentioned.
quote: For information about which operating systems are compatible with Mobile VPN with SSL, see the Operating System Compatibility list in the Fireware Release Notes.

claim: WatchGuard officially supports connecting to Mobile VPN with SSL from a third-party OpenVPN client using a client.ovpn profile downloaded from the Firebox, including two-factor challenge-response on Fireware v12.3+.
quote: make an SSL VPN connection to the Firebox with an OpenVPN client ... Mobile VPN with SSL supports two-factor, challenge-response authentication for native OpenVPN clients

claim: A community walkthrough exists for importing the WatchGuard client.ovpn profile into a Linux OpenVPN/NetworkManager setup.
quote: The different certificates are stored inside the OpenVPN client configuration file. So, either you leave it as-is or you might consider to cut the certificates from the file and store them as individual files.

claim: Check Point Harmony SASE ships an official Linux SASE Agent: Ubuntu 20.04+ deb, Red Hat 8+ rpm, Fedora 40+ rpm, and a generic tar.xz.
quote: Ubuntu 20.04 or later (Deb package); Red Hat 8 or later (RPM package); Fedora 40 or later (RPM Fedora package); Generic Linux 8.0 or later (tar.xz archive)

claim: Harmony SASE Posture Check runs client-side and blocks private access when the device fails the configured posture requirements, re-evaluated periodically.
quote: if the device does not meet the specified posture requirement, then the SASE Agent blocks private access. The posture check is performed periodically while the device is connected

claim: LenovoLegionLinux replaces the useful parts of Lenovo Vantage/Legion Zone on Linux — fan curves, power modes, power limits, rapid charge, battery conservation, Y-logo LED — but fan control is unverified on gen-8 (2023) and newer models, and it delegates 4-zone RGB to a separate project.
quote: It is the alternative to Lenovo Vantage or Legion Zone (both Windows only). ... 4 Zone RGB backlight: please use https://github.com/4JX/L5P-Keyboard-RGB

claim: Lenovo's WMI gaming-series drivers were merged for mainline Linux 6.17, exposing Quiet/Balanced/Performance power modes through power-profiles-daemon, Fn+Q or sysfs.
quote: Derek Clark has been leading the effort on the Lenovo WMI Gaming Series Drivers since last year and they appear ready to cross the milestone of going into the mainline Linux kernel.

claim: L5P-Keyboard-RGB controls the 4-zone RGB keyboard on Legion 5/5 Pro/Slim and LOQ 2020-2024 under Linux (root or udev rule), but Legion 7(i) per-key backlights and white-only backlights are unsupported.
quote: Legion 7(i): Won't work, the backlight on these is per-key and uses a different way of communicating

claim: There is no Intel-endorsed CPU undervolting path on Linux; intel-undervolt and similar tools are unofficial MSR-based hacks and the voltage interface is locked by firmware on many recent Intel systems.
quote: currently on Linux there isn't any Intel-endorsed way for undervolting your CPU ... There exists the intel-undervolt program that is unofficial and developed by an independent developer

claim: HeadsetControl's supported-device table covers Logitech, Corsair, SteelSeries, HyperX, ROCCAT, Audeze, Sony and others but does not include JBL Quantum headsets.
quote: Supported devices: Logitech, Corsair, SteelSeries, HyperX, ROCCAT, Audeze, Lenovo, Plantronics, Sony

claim: JBL QuantumENGINE is offered for Windows, macOS, iOS and Android only.
quote: JBL QuantumENGINE is refreshed with a new unified streamlined interface that works across Windows, macOS, iOS and Android devices

claim: EasyEffects provides equalizer, convolver, limiter, compressor, loudness and related effects as native PipeWire filters, covering the EQ role that vendor headset software plays on Windows.
quote: Limiter, compressor, convolver, equalizer and auto volume and many other plugins for PipeWire applications

claim: speaker-tuning-to-easyeffects converts the DAX3 Dolby Atmos speaker-tuning XML embedded in OEM Windows audio drivers into an EasyEffects preset or a headless PipeWire filter-chain, with Lenovo models among those confirmed.
quote: Convert OEM Dolby Atmos speaker tuning data to EasyEffects presets or PipeWire filter-chain for Linux

claim: Intel provides no Linux drivers for Intel Killer wireless products and directs Linux users to the generic Intel wireless driver (iwlwifi) for the equivalent adapter.
quote: Intel doesn't provide Linux drivers for Intel Killer Wireless Products, but we recommend using generic Linux Wireless drivers, which are available for Intel Wireless products.

claim: Intel has no plans to release Arc Control for non-Windows operating systems.
quote: There are currently no plans to release Arc Control on non-Windows operating systems.

claim: Driverless printing (IPP Everywhere / AirPrint / Mopria) with cups, cups-filters, cups-browsed and ipp-usb sets up modern printers with no vendor driver or PPD.
quote: Driverless printing for CUPS and cups-filters is here to stay

claim: Epson publishes ESC/P-R printer drivers and Epson Scan 2 for Linux as unsupported .deb/.rpm packages, with the ESC/P-R Linux manual revised in early 2026.
quote: Epson does not provide support for Linux drivers, though Linux drivers are available for some products

claim: webOS Dev Manager publishes x86_64 and ARM64 .deb and AppImage builds for Linux alongside the Windows and macOS installers.
quote: Windows, Linux and macOS (Apple Silicon too!)
